name: MD-08
label: Safe D

key_factors: District's D+30 partisan lean makes it deeply Democratic territory
Raskin holds a massive financial edge: $7.9M on hand vs. Riley's $2.7K
Well-known incumbent seeking reelection with no expert ratings flagging the race
Prediction markets price the contest near 98-2 for Democrats
model.rationale: The district's thirty-point Democratic lean, Raskin's overwhelming cash advantage over a challenger who has raised about $22,000, and markets pricing the race near 98-2 leave no plausible path for Riley; the only real uncertainty is the size of the margin.
model.watch: Only an extraordinary late development, such as a major scandal or sudden heavy outside spending against Raskin, would put the outcome in doubt, and nothing in the evidence suggests one is coming.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview: Maryland's 8th District sits deep in Democratic territory, with a partisan lean of roughly thirty points, and Jamie Raskin has held the seat comfortably. He returns this year with one of the largest war chests in the House, having raised more than nine million dollars and holding nearly eight million on hand. Republican Cheryl Riley has reported about twenty-two thousand dollars raised and under three thousand in cash, leaving little capacity to introduce herself to voters. A Green Party candidate is also on the ballot, but with no polling, no outside spending, and no expert ratings flagging the race, there is little sign of competition. Prediction markets put Democratic odds near ninety-eight percent. Everything points to Raskin winning another term by a wide margin, with the main question being the size of the victory.
